source_name: ADP — Arhiv družboslovnih podatkov (Social Science Data Archive, FDV Ljubljana)
why_relevant: National social-science data archive holding ~600 collections including deposited SURS survey data (e.g. historical APG waves) with rich study-level documentation. Valuable for long back-series and for reconstructing question wording on payment/consumption items.

source_name: SURS Podjetja (Enterprises) statistical field — SiStat area
why_relevant: Structural business statistics and enterprise demography by NACE, giving counts and turnover of retail, hospitality and services enterprises — the merchant-population denominator for POS terminal penetration estimates.

source_name: SURS methodological explanations and quality reports (Metodološka pojasnila / Poročila o kakovosti)
why_relevant: Defines exactly what each indicator covers, break-in-series dates (e.g. COICOP 1999 to COICOP 2018 switch), sample design and known quality limitations. Essential to avoid mis-normalising payment data against a redefined denominator.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Register plačilnih institucij (Register of payment institutions)
why_relevant: Dedicated statutory register (under ZPlaSSIED) of payment institutions licensed by Banka Slovenije, incl. those with waiver/exemption, their agents and branches. Directly names the non-bank PSP population Printec would sell to.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Register družb za izdajo elektronskega denarja (E-money institutions register)
why_relevant: Central database of e-money institutions (incl. hybrid EMIs), their representatives in SI and host states, branches in host and third countries, plus entities whose authorisation has lapsed. Captures the fastest-moving licensed segment (e.g. Paywiser) and cross-border passporting footprint.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Plačilne institucije držav EGP v Sloveniji (EEA payment institutions passporting into Slovenia)
why_relevant: Enumerates foreign EEA payment institutions operating in Slovenia via branch, agent or freedom of services — a population invisible in AJPES because they have no Slovenian filed accounts. Essential to size the true competitive field for acquiring and payment services.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Seznam notifikacij plačilnih institucij (PDF notification list)
why_relevant: Periodically republished PDF listing notifications received from home-state competent authorities for payment institutions serving Slovenia. Dated filenames make it a good longitudinal series for tracking inbound market entry.

source_name: AJPES – ePRS, Poslovni register Slovenije (Slovenian Business Register search)
why_relevant: Central public database of every business entity registered in Slovenia, freely accessible since 17 Oct 2014. Lets you resolve a licensed PSP name to matricna stevilka (registration no.), tax no., NACE/SKD activity, address, representatives and owners — the join key between the BS licence registers and filed financial statements. Also allows SKD-activity sweeps to find ATM/POS servicing companies that hold no payment licence.

source_name: AJPES – Koledar javne objave letnih poročil (annual report publication calendar)
why_relevant: States the exact dates each filing cohort becomes public, which lets the collection routine schedule its annual pull precisely instead of polling blindly. Also flags which entity types (banks, insurers, cooperatives, sole traders) publish when.

source_name: AJPES – Uradne objave / eObjave vpisov v poslovni in sodni register (court & business register gazette)
why_relevant: Publishes every court-register entry (Srg), founding document and change of capital, ownership, name or representatives, with underlying documents published since 1 Feb 2008 and accessible for one year. This is the earliest public signal of a new payments entity, a capital injection into an ATM deployer, or an acquisition — months before it shows in annual accounts.

source_name: AJPES – Register dejanskih lastnikov (RDL, beneficial ownership register)
why_relevant: Ultimate-beneficial-owner data for Slovenian business entities under ZPPDFT-1; would reveal who actually controls small PSPs, ATM deployers and terminal resellers. Access, however, was materially narrowed as of 09.08.2025 following ZPPDFT-1 amendments, so it is a conditional rather than open source.

source_name: AJPES – Bonitete / FI=PO Finančni pomočnik and S.BON credit-rating products
why_relevant: AJPES value-added layer over the same filings: benchmarking ratios, sector aggregates and S.BON scores. Useful for placing a Slovenian PSP or ATM operator against its SKD-sector peer distribution without rebuilding the ratio maths, and for spotting financially stressed independent deployers.

source_name: AJPES – Predložitev letnih poročil: obligations and filing rules pages
why_relevant: Defines exactly which entity classes must file, on what forms, and with what audit obligations — the metadata needed to know whether a given payments actor's absence from JOLP means 'not required to file' rather than 'does not exist'. Prevents false negatives in coverage counts.

source_name: EBA EUCLID – Payment Institutions Register (PIR), Slovenia subset
why_relevant: EU-wide central register of payment and e-money institutions built from national competent-authority feeds, with institution name, country, competent authority, authorisation status and the specific payment services offered. Serves as an independent cross-check on the Banka Slovenije registers and, crucially, standardises PSD2 service codes so Slovenian actors are comparable with regional peers.

source_name: EBA – Credit Institutions Register and 'Other list of institutions'
why_relevant: Authoritative list of authorised credit institutions per EEA state, downloadable in bulk. Gives the Slovenian bank population (the dominant ATM and POS acquiring owners) in a comparable format, and the 'other list' catches entities in adjacent regimes.

source_name: GVIN.com – Slovenian business intelligence and financial analysis database
why_relevant: Higher-end commercial layer over Slovenian company and financial data with multi-year analysis packages (reported tiers c. EUR 1,505 / 1,999 / 2,800 + VAT annually). Relevant if the project needs multi-year peer analytics for PSPs and terminal/ATM service firms without building the ratio pipeline in-house.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Poročilo o delovanju plačilnega sistema (payment system operation reporting page)
why_relevant: Defines the mandatory reporting that licensed payment system operators and PSPs must submit to Banka Slovenije, including the report templates and schedules. Not a register itself, but it tells you which volume and value datapoints legally exist per licensed actor — the roadmap for what the statistics cells can hope to obtain.

source_name: Portal javnih naročil (enarocanje.si) — official Slovenian public procurement portal
why_relevant: Statutory national publication point for all Slovenian contract notices and contract award notices (obvestila o oddaji naročila), operated by the Directorate for Public Procurement (Direktorat za javno naročanje, MJU). This is where ATM purchase/maintenance, POS terminal, cash-in-transit (prevoz in varovanje gotovine), card issuing and core banking tenders by Slovenian public bodies and state-owned entities must appear. Award notices carry contract value, winning bidder and often quantities (number of terminals/ATMs).

source_name: e-JN — Elektronsko javno naročanje (ejn.gov.si), incl. 'Aktualna javna naročila' listing
why_relevant: Slovenia's e-procurement transaction system (submission, e-opening, e-catalogues). Its 'Aktualna javna naročila' page lists live tenders with contracting authority, subject, deadlines and opening dates — the earliest signal that a bank/ATM/POS/CIT contract is coming to market, ahead of award publication.

source_name: OPSI — Evidenca javnih naročil (open dataset of Slovenian public procurement records)
why_relevant: Machine-readable national open-data dump of procurement records from 1 Jan 2013 onward: contracting authority (name, region), procedure (subject, legal basis, procedure type) and bidder (name, country, region). This is the single best bulk-quantitative entry point for building a Slovenian ATM/POS/CIT/core-banking contract dataset without scraping.

source_name: OPSI — Aktualna javna naročila v informacijskem sistemu e-JN (dataset resource)
why_relevant: Structured feed of currently open tenders (authority, title, code, publication timestamp, portal reference number, submission deadline, opening date, status) — the automatable version of the e-JN listing for pipeline monitoring of ATM/POS/CIT lots.

source_name: OPSI — Pregled objavljenih pogodb po oddaji javnega naročila (published post-award contracts)
why_relevant: Under the access-to-public-information law, contracting authorities must publish the actual signed contracts following award. This gives contract text — not just the notice — which is where terminal counts, ATM fleet sizes, SLA terms, unit prices and contract duration for ATM maintenance / CIT / POS deals actually live.

source_name: STATIST — OPSI public procurement statistics application
why_relevant: Analytical front-end over Slovenian procurement data from 2013 onward: largest contracting authorities, largest winning bidders, most frequent procurement subjects. Useful for ranking vendors (incl. security/CIT firms and IT integrators serving banks) and for sizing categories quickly before deep extraction.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU supplement), Slovenia notices
why_relevant: All above-threshold Slovenian contract and award notices are mirrored to TED in structured eForms/XML with CPV codes, values and awarded-supplier data. TED is the cleanest cross-border comparator: it lets Slovenian ATM/POS/CIT/core-banking awards be benchmarked against neighbouring markets using the same CPV taxonomy.

source_name: TED Search API (docs.ted.europa.eu)
why_relevant: Documented, authentication-free read API for querying TED notices with expert query syntax. The technically correct collection channel for a repeatable Slovenian banking/payments procurement dataset.

source_name: TED XML bulk download (daily/monthly packages) + TED FTP archive
why_relevant: Full historical corpus of EU notices in XML (archive reportedly back to 1993 via FTP with guest credentials). Enables longitudinal reconstruction of Slovenian ATM/POS/CIT contract cycles and incumbent rotation over decades — not obtainable from any vendor-published material.

source_name: TED Open Data Service (SPARQL / RDF)
why_relevant: Semantic access to the whole TED corpus; SPARQL queries can extract custom cross-notice datasets (e.g. all SI awards under banking/ATM CPVs with values and suppliers) far more cheaply than scraping HTML notices.
